narrative.overview:
AiFoundIt deliberately follows familiar AI-chat conventions — the Gemini/ChatGPT/Claude pattern — rather than a distinctive visual concept, and the entire design effort goes into executing that canon at high craft. The warmth the user asked for comes from a warm-neutral stone palette and a single deep amber accent, not from decoration. There is no AI sparkle, no gradient, no glow; the craft lives in spacing, type scale, state behavior, and honest copy.

The system is a React Native implementation of Material 3, expressed as a JS theme object with paired light and dark palettes consumed through role names. Surfaces layer tonally; outlined cards carry structure instead of shadows. Copy does design work: privacy promises are stated plainly, index state is shown honestly, and the demo is labeled as sample data.
keyCharacteristics: Single deep amber accent reserved for send, primary actions, selection, and progress
Warm-neutral stone surface ramp, tonal layering instead of shadows
Roboto (platform sans-serif) on the Material 3 type scale — no display face
Pill-shaped buttons and list items; outlined file and suggestion cards
Chat asymmetry: user turns in tonal bubbles, assistant turns as plain text with cards
Material Symbols icons; state communicated through Android ripples and snackbar feedback

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber primary is reserved for send, primary actions, selection, progress, and the confirming check. It is never decoration, never a large fill, never a background tint on its own. If a new screen needs emphasis, reach for tonal surfaces first.

rules.name: The Ramp, Not the Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is conveyed by stepping up the surface ramp and outlining with Stone Line — not by elevation. New surfaces pick a ramp step, not a shadow.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: Type comes from the platform (sans-serif / sans-serif-medium on Android, system default elsewhere). No bundled display face, no brand font. Icons are Material Symbols; they are iconography, not a typeface decision.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: UI text runs at 400 or 500 only. A lone 600 appears inside simulated file-thumbnail previews, where it imitates app content rather than UI chrome.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and in state. Press feedback is an Android ripple tinted with Stone Line — not a lift. If content must overlay the canvas, use a sheet or snackbar, not a floating card.

dos: Do reserve Deep Amber for send, primary actions, selection, and progress — tonal surfaces do the rest of the work.
Do outline cards with a 1px Stone Line border on the paper surface instead of adding elevation.
Do state privacy and data status in plain Body Small copy ('This preview uses sample files', 'Still indexing, so some files may not show up yet') — honesty is a visual element here.
Do honor reduced motion: entry animations (280ms fade-and-rise, sheet slide) drop to instant when the system requests it.
Do pick surface steps off the ramp by role — sheets/drawers/proposals on Low, composer and bubbles on High, disabled fills on Highest.
donts: Don't add decorative AI effects — no sparkle icons, gradients, glows, shimmer skeletons, or branded mascot moments; the chosen direction is the category standard.
Don't introduce shadows on cards, buttons, or bars — the snackbar is the sole shadowed element.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or a display typeface; the system is one amber plus stone, one platform sans.

Don't treat the current app icon, adaptive icon background (#E6F4FE), or splash screen (#208AEF) as palette — they are Expo template defaults disclosed in PRODUCT.md, a known carry-over awaiting brand assets, not design decisions.
Don't auto-emphasize with caps or heavy weights; UI type stays at 400/500, and destructive or relocating actions always present a confirm affordance, never just styling.
